evidence_required: FT-007-AC-001 RED: the client records response receipt locally but the core Attempt has no response_received_ms column or authenticated report boundary, so a server-visible timeline cannot distinguish the browser receipt from server response time; GREEN: the next linear migration, promo repository and exact authenticated endpoint store the first ordered browser monotonic response marker for result, zero-proposal, busy, deadline and admitted technical-failure Attempts, derive bounded issue/gap tags, preserve an equal repeat and reject a conflicting/foreign report without changing outcome/session/display truth; decisive comparison: controlled client clock, scoped HTTP response and disposable persisted Attempt before/after first, equal, conflicting and missing reports; artifact: migration/API/client evidence under .tasks/TASK-083-T3-FT-007-W1/.

FT-007-AC-005 RED_NOT_APPLICABLE: the accepted offline claim is already true before this task, and inducing a missing core Attempt after admission or adding a durable pre-admission outbox merely to obtain RED would falsify the accepted behavior; alternative proof: preserve the current pre-admission no-row and post-admission retained-outcome behavior, then prove the new best-effort timing report neither creates an Attempt nor becomes a participant-flow prerequisite; decisive comparison: controlled disconnect before and after admission plus server row count/outcome and client event trace; artifact: focused offline/timing integration evidence under .tasks/TASK-083-T3-FT-007-W1/.
purpose: Complete the promo-owned core Attempt timeline with the browser response-receipt marker while preserving best-effort offline semantics and the accepted display-client security boundary.
success_outcome: Every exercised admitted outcome retains one core Attempt with an ordered client response marker when reported and an explicit gap when absent, while pre-admission offline delivery may leave no row and no timing-report failure changes participant truth.
anti_goals: Do not add a reliable client outbox, replay queue, replacement Attempt, distributed tracing or client/server clock subtraction.
Do not write diagnostics-owned evidence, implement the Attempts UI or change result/session/display state.
Do not rotate credentials, log timing bodies/tokens or add a second authentication mechanism.

forbidden_scope: Production display-client credentials, operator/default Attempts and unredacted request evidence
Diagnostics evidence tables, retention deletion, FT-008 investigation UI and FT-009 logs
FT-005 display transition semantics and FT-006 browser-access state beyond consuming their completed migration/result
stop_conditions: The response marker cannot remain a promo-owned first-write transition on the existing core Attempt.
A correct report would require a reliable queue, client/server wall-clock subtraction or a new public identity scheme.
The migration cannot follow the actual direct Alembic predecessor without rewriting another task's revision.
Security probes cannot use disposable scoped display clients and Attempts with safe cleanup.

constraints: Primary state owner is promo; the realtime handler authenticates and serializes but never writes the core table outside the repository.
Use the current display-client token hash to derive spa_id, return the same non-disclosing unknown/foreign result, rate-limit the route and emit no-store responses.
Use one client monotonic origin and require response_received_ms >= request_started_ms; never synthesize the marker from server time.
Use uniquely identified task-owned display clients and Attempts with known initial state, controlled clocks, safe rerun, decisive state reads and cleanup limited to those fixtures.
Resolve the migration's actual direct predecessor at execution; verify only this revision's upgrade/downgrade/re-upgrade and data preservation, not a mutable exact head.
invariants: Only promo mutates the core Attempt; diagnostics and the HTTP adapter never write it directly.
The first valid response marker is immutable, equal repeat is idempotent and conflict/foreign/invalid input changes nothing.
Missing best-effort timing stays an explicit gap and never changes the terminal participant outcome.
Credentials, request bodies and protected identifiers never enter logs or retained task artifacts.
verification_targets: Controlled-clock migration/repository/API/client fixtures prove ordered timing for result, zero-proposal, busy, deadline and admitted technical failure, first/equal/conflicting behavior and explicit missing-report gaps.
Disconnect fixtures compare pre-admission no-row behavior with post-admission retained core outcome and prove the timing sender adds no upsert, retry queue or participant-flow dependency.
T3 scope/redaction checks use only disposable principals/rows, prove token-derived spa isolation, 401/404/409/422/429 behavior, no-store responses and complete fixture cleanup.
